teaching_examples.text: Se fæder sægde: ‘Ic eom hēr.’ Se fæder sægde ðæt hē ðǣr wǣre.
teaching_examples.translation: The father said, 'I am here.' The father said that he was there.
teaching_examples.pedagogical_purpose: The same speaker becomes third person in a report; here/there assumes that the reporter is speaking from another place.
teaching_examples.display_obligation: Print the complete Old English, translation and bounded point after the relevant forms, senses and frames have been made available.

teaching_examples.text: Hē geseah ðone mann cuman. Hē wiste ðæt se mann cōme.
teaching_examples.translation: He saw the man come. He knew that the man came.
teaching_examples.pedagogical_purpose: The perceived actor is accusative with an infinitive; the finite content-clause subject is nominative. The second sentence uses the reported subjunctive.

teaching_examples.text: Gē cunnon ðone cyning; gē cunnon singan.
teaching_examples.translation: You know the king; you know how to sing.
teaching_examples.pedagogical_purpose: The new personal-acquaintance sense takes a person as object; the prior skill sense takes a plain infinitive. Witan can also take a person, as Cook35.7 shows; this is not an exclusive lexical partition.

teaching_examples.text: Hē plegode wel, and hīe dydon swā.
teaching_examples.translation: He played well, and they did so.
teaching_examples.pedagogical_purpose: Dōn recovers the preceding playing action while retaining its own subject and number.
